The cleanest fix that matches the behavior of the development DB is: in the production DB, make sure pg_trgm/unaccent are also available in `public` (matching the development DB), so that the schema load works. But since they already exist in shared_extensions, CREATE EXTENSION will be skipped.

Let me set the search_path of the consul_production database to include shared_extensions so that gin_trgm_ops can be resolved. This aligns with the intent of the guide (extensions inside a dedicated schema). I'll set the default search_path.

Actually, the guide says to place the extensions in the `shared_extensions` schema. So the app should be able to find them. The reason the development DB has them in `public` is an accident of my setup. To make the production environment work as intended (extensions in shared_extensions), I should set the database's search_path to include shared_extensions.

Let me set the default search_path of the consul_production database.

action.command: export PGPASSWORD=root; psql -h localhost -U root -d consul_production -c "ALTER DATABASE consul_production SET search_path TO public, shared_extensions;" 2>&1; echo "--- verify ---"; psql -h localhost -U root -d consul_production -t -c "show search_path;"
